findings.description: The bucket is explicitly commented as public with no ACL restricting access, allowing anyone to read or write objects including sensitive customer data.
No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined, so objects stored in the bucket are not encrypted at rest.
Versioning is not enabled, which combined with public access and force_destroy increases risk of data loss, tampering, or ransomware-style overwrite attacks going unnoticed.
A sensitive file (customer-master.xlsx) is uploaded to the aws_s3_bucket.data bucket which is public and unencrypted, exposing customer data to unauthorized access.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined for this bucket holding financial data, leaving objects unencrypted at rest.
Versioning is not enabled, increasing risk of unrecoverable data loss or tampering for financial records, especially combined with force_destroy.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined, so operational data stored in this bucket is not encrypted at rest.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined, leaving data science bucket contents unencrypted at rest.
